what: Elbit Systems is Israel's largest defence company. It makes drones, artillery and rocket systems, electro-optics and night vision, helmet-mounted displays for fighter pilots, electronic warfare systems and ammunition.
customers: The Israeli Ministry of Defense, European and Asian governments, and the US defence market through its American subsidiary.
money: command and control systems and communications
artillery, ammunition and armoured vehicle systems
moat: Combat-proven systems tested in actual use, which European buyers rebuilding their armies value, combined with a cost base below large US primes.
risks: Some European governments have faced political pressure to limit Israeli defence purchases
Gross margin of 24% is modest and operating margin is 8%
Production capacity has been stretched by wartime demand
It depends heavily on government budget cycles
opportunities: Revenue grew about 16% last year and about 13% a year over three years
European rearmament has produced a record order backlog
Drones and precision munitions, where it is strong, are the fastest-growing defence categories
watch: The order backlog and new European contract wins.
